messages.text:
The first compare exposed a few useful parser bugs rather than broad design problems: hyphenated operators were being split, bare command arguments like filenames were being treated as cell paths, and dot/range tokenization was too greedy.

I’m patching those now, plus making `ls` ignore dotfiles like Nushell does by default.

commands.commandLine:
"C:\\Program Files\\PowerShell\\7\\pwsh.exe" -Command '$env:PYTHONIOENCODING='"'utf-8'; @'
import subprocess, pathlib, sys, os
nu=pathlib.Path('REFERENCE_BINARY.txt').read_text().strip()
py=[sys.executable,'nushell_port.py']
cases=['1 + 2','16 bit-shr 1','5 bit-shl 1','2 bit-shl 1 + 2','10 - 2 bit-shr 2','4 bit-xor 4',\"'d' not-in 'abc'\",'1..3','1..<3','[[a,b]; [1,2] [3,4]] | get a',r\"{'a': 'b'} | get a\",r\"{'b': 'c'}.b\",r\"'hello world' | split column ' ' | get column1\",'open REFERENCE_BINARY.txt | lines | length','[[a b]; [jim susie] [3 4]] | to json -r',r\"{foo: {bar: '[{\\\"a\\\":\\\"b\\\",\\\"c\\\": 2}]'}} | to json --raw\",'ls | length']
for c in cases:
    r=subprocess.run([nu,'-c',c],capture_output=True,text=True,encoding='utf-8',errors='replace')
    p=subprocess.run(py+['-c',c],capture_output=True,text=True,encoding='utf-8',errors='replace')
    if (r.returncode,r.stdout,r.stderr)"'!=(p.returncode,p.stdout,p.stderr):
        print('"'MISMATCH',c)
        print('REF',r.returncode,repr(r.stdout),repr(r.stderr[:200]))
        print('PY ',p.returncode,repr(p.stdout),repr(p.stderr[:200]))
'@ | python -"
